A fine-art photograph on medium-format colour film, bright high summer noon light, golden wheat and deep blue sky. In the middle of a wide ripe wheat field stands a worn green velvet armchair, a small wooden side table with an open book and a cup, and a tall standard lamp with a fabric shade that is switched on and glowing weakly in daylight, its flex trailing into the wheat. The wheat reaches the seat of the chair. No people, no house in sight, a flat horizon. Everything else is ordinary and real.

A flat two-colour screenprint illustration in dark bottle green and warm cream only, no shading, gradients or outlines, faint paper grain. A single tall cream chess pawn stands upright in the exact centre, filling the full height of the frame, on a dark green ground. Its left and right contours are drawn so that the two green spaces beside it read equally as two human faces in profile facing each other: the pawn's round head forms the space between two foreheads, its neck collar the noses, its narrow waist the lips and chins, its wide base the necks and shoulders. Both readings must be equally strong: a pawn, or two faces nearly touching. Perfectly symmetrical, nothing else in the picture.
